title: IL SB1920: SCH CD-ASL IMPLEMENTATION

obligations: The State Board of Education shall develop statewide guidance for school districts and educators on the use of artificial intelligence in elementary and secondary education, in consultation with stakeholders, including specified topics (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)).
The State Board of Education shall develop and publish this guidance by July 1, 2026 and provide continuous updates as it deems necessary (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)).

If the State Superintendent convenes a statewide council on AI, the council must include individuals with expertise in artificial intelligence and no fewer than 2 currently practicing classroom teachers, and must represent ethnic, racial, and geographic diversity and include expertise across early childhood, elementary, middle, and high school settings (Sec. 2-3.118a(b)).
No later than July 1, 2026, the State Board of Education shall encourage school districts to collect teaching resources to support American Sign Language programs (Sec. 2-3.206).

The State Board of Education, in consultation with the State Educator Preparation and Licensure Board, shall design and implement a system of examinations required prior to the issuance of educator licenses (Sec. 21B-30(b)).
The State Board must adopt rules to implement a paraprofessional competency test (Sec. 21B-30(c-5)).

All applicants seeking a State license shall be required to pass a test of content area knowledge for each area of endorsement for which there is an applicable test, with no exception (Sec. 21B-30(d)).

The State Board shall consult with applicable vendors within 90 days after July 28, 2023 to develop a plan to transition the elementary education content area test by July 1, 2026 to include bilingualism, biliteracy, oral language development, foundational literacy skills, and developmentally appropriate higher-order comprehension (Sec. 21B-30(d-5)).

Beginning on September 1, 2025, all candidates completing teacher preparation programs and all candidates subject to Section 21B-35 are required to pass a teacher performance assessment approved by the State Board (Sec. 21B-30(f)).

The Teacher Performance Assessment Task Force shall report on its work, including recommendations, to the State Board of Education and the General Assembly on or before October 31, 2024 (Sec. 21B-30(f-5)).

The content area knowledge test and teacher performance assessment shall be tests designated by the State Board, must be designed to be racially neutral, and shall be administered not fewer than 3 times a year (Sec. 21B-30(g)).

The State Board shall implement a test or tests to assess speaking, reading, writing, and grammar skills of applicants for certain endorsements or licenses in English and in the language of the transitional bilingual education program (Sec. 21B-30(g)).

On or before July 1, 2026, the State Board of Education shall post publicly on its website the process by which the State Board or any designated entity evaluates content area knowledge tests to determine content validity, an absence of bias, or the scores required to pass, and shall make publicly available the process for selecting committee members and the agenda and summary of each meeting (Sec. 21B-30(g-5)).

The rules developed to implement and enforce testing requirements shall include provisions governing test selection, validation, passing score, administration, frequency, applicant fees, frequency of applicants taking tests, years for which a score is valid, and appropriate special accommodations (Sec. 21B-30(i)).

Beginning with the 2009-2010 school year, a school district must incorporate into the school curriculum a component on Internet safety to be taught at least once each school year to students in grades 3 through 12, with the school board determining scope and duration (Sec. 27-13.3(c)).

The State Board of Education shall make available resource materials for educating children regarding child online safety and shall make these resource materials available on its Internet website (Sec. 27-13.3(e)).
prohibitions: A candidate may not be required to submit test materials by video submission (Sec. 21B-30(f)).

There shall be no exception to the requirement that all applicants seeking a State license pass a test of content area knowledge for each area of endorsement for which there is an applicable test (Sec. 21B-30(d)).

It also requires school districts to include in their Internet safety curriculum a component on recognizing and reporting online harassment and cyber-bullying, including false representations created by artificial intelligence such as sexually explicit images and videos. The law also addresses American Sign Language teaching resources and educator testing requirements.

Ensure that any AI tools used in elementary and secondary education are evaluated for bias, privacy, transparency, and risk, and comply with federal and State student data privacy laws listed in the guidance (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)(3)-(4)).

Incorporate into the school district's Internet safety curriculum a component on recognizing and reporting online harassment and cyber-bullying, including AI-created false representations such as sexually explicit images and videos, taught at least once each school year to grades 3 through 12 (Sec. 27-13.3(c)(5)).

If using AI in educator testing or content area knowledge tests, monitor the State Board's website for the posted evaluation process by July 1, 2026 and ensure tests are racially neutral and meet content validity and bias standards (Sec. 21B-30(g), (g-5)).

how_it_affects_ai_deployment: School districts must include in their Internet safety curriculum a component on recognizing and reporting online harassment and cyber-bullying, including the creation and distribution of false representations of individuals created by artificial intelligence, including sexually explicit images and videos, taught at least once each school year to grades 3 through 12 (Sec. 27-13.3(c)(5)).

The State Board of Education will publish statewide guidance on AI use in elementary and secondary education by July 1, 2026, covering bias, privacy, transparency, risk assessment and management, student data privacy laws, and best practices, which school districts and educators should follow when deploying AI (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)).
The State Board may convene a statewide council with AI expertise and at least 2 practicing classroom teachers to further develop guidance and resources for AI use in schools (Sec. 2-3.118a(b)).

Organisations deploying AI in schools should consider the State Board's resource materials on child online safety, which may include topics like privacy protection and cyber-bullying (Sec. 27-13.3(e)).

Passed 2025-08-15. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

The law requires the Illinois State Board of Education to develop and publish statewide guidance on the use of artificial intelligence in elementary and secondary education by July 1, 2026, covering topics such as bias, privacy, transparency, risk, and student data privacy. It also requires school districts to include in their Internet safety curriculum a component on recognizing and reporting online harassment and cyber-bullying, including false representations created by artificial intelligence such as sexually explicit images and videos. The law also addresses American Sign Language teaching resources and educator testing requirements.

Who it applies to

  • Illinois State Board of Education
  • School districts
  • Educators
  • Candidates for educator licenses
  • State Superintendent of Education

Effective date

not stated in the text

Obligations

  • The State Board of Education shall develop statewide guidance for school districts and educators on the use of artificial intelligence in elementary and secondary education, in consultation with stakeholders, including specified topics (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)).
  • The State Board of Education shall develop and publish this guidance by July 1, 2026 and provide continuous updates as it deems necessary (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)).
  • If the State Superintendent convenes a statewide council on AI, the council must include individuals with expertise in artificial intelligence and no fewer than 2 currently practicing classroom teachers, and must represent ethnic, racial, and geographic diversity and include expertise across early childhood, elementary, middle, and high school settings (Sec. 2-3.118a(b)).
  • No later than July 1, 2026, the State Board of Education shall encourage school districts to collect teaching resources to support American Sign Language programs (Sec. 2-3.206).
  • The State Board of Education, in consultation with the State Educator Preparation and Licensure Board, shall design and implement a system of examinations required prior to the issuance of educator licenses (Sec. 21B-30(b)).
  • The State Board must adopt rules to implement a paraprofessional competency test (Sec. 21B-30(c-5)).
  • All applicants seeking a State license shall be required to pass a test of content area knowledge for each area of endorsement for which there is an applicable test, with no exception (Sec. 21B-30(d)).
  • The State Board shall consult with applicable vendors within 90 days after July 28, 2023 to develop a plan to transition the elementary education content area test by July 1, 2026 to include bilingualism, biliteracy, oral language development, foundational literacy skills, and developmentally appropriate higher-order comprehension (Sec. 21B-30(d-5)).
  • Beginning on September 1, 2025, all candidates completing teacher preparation programs and all candidates subject to Section 21B-35 are required to pass a teacher performance assessment approved by the State Board (Sec. 21B-30(f)).
  • The Teacher Performance Assessment Task Force shall report on its work, including recommendations, to the State Board of Education and the General Assembly on or before October 31, 2024 (Sec. 21B-30(f-5)).
  • The content area knowledge test and teacher performance assessment shall be tests designated by the State Board, must be designed to be racially neutral, and shall be administered not fewer than 3 times a year (Sec. 21B-30(g)).
  • The State Board shall implement a test or tests to assess speaking, reading, writing, and grammar skills of applicants for certain endorsements or licenses in English and in the language of the transitional bilingual education program (Sec. 21B-30(g)).
  • On or before July 1, 2026, the State Board of Education shall post publicly on its website the process by which the State Board or any designated entity evaluates content area knowledge tests to determine content validity, an absence of bias, or the scores required to pass, and shall make publicly available the process for selecting committee members and the agenda and summary of each meeting (Sec. 21B-30(g-5)).
  • The rules developed to implement and enforce testing requirements shall include provisions governing test selection, validation, passing score, administration, frequency, applicant fees, frequency of applicants taking tests, years for which a score is valid, and appropriate special accommodations (Sec. 21B-30(i)).
  • Beginning with the 2009-2010 school year, a school district must incorporate into the school curriculum a component on Internet safety to be taught at least once each school year to students in grades 3 through 12, with the school board determining scope and duration (Sec. 27-13.3(c)).
  • The State Board of Education shall make available resource materials for educating children regarding child online safety and shall make these resource materials available on its Internet website (Sec. 27-13.3(e)).

Prohibitions

  • A candidate may not be required to submit test materials by video submission (Sec. 21B-30(f)).
  • There shall be no exception to the requirement that all applicants seeking a State license pass a test of content area knowledge for each area of endorsement for which there is an applicable test (Sec. 21B-30(d)).

Penalties and enforcement

Not stated in the text. The State Board of Education develops guidance and rules (Sec. 2-3.118a, Sec. 21B-30), and curricula may be submitted for review to the Office of the Illinois Attorney General (Sec. 27-13.3(d)), but no penalties, enforcement authority, or private right of action are specified.

How it affects AI deployment

  • School districts must include in their Internet safety curriculum a component on recognizing and reporting online harassment and cyber-bullying, including the creation and distribution of false representations of individuals created by artificial intelligence, including sexually explicit images and videos, taught at least once each school year to grades 3 through 12 (Sec. 27-13.3(c)(5)).
  • The State Board of Education will publish statewide guidance on AI use in elementary and secondary education by July 1, 2026, covering bias, privacy, transparency, risk assessment and management, student data privacy laws, and best practices, which school districts and educators should follow when deploying AI (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)).
  • The State Board may convene a statewide council with AI expertise and at least 2 practicing classroom teachers to further develop guidance and resources for AI use in schools (Sec. 2-3.118a(b)).
  • If an organisation deploys AI in educator testing or content area knowledge tests, it must be aware that the State Board will post by July 1, 2026 the process for evaluating tests for content validity, absence of bias, and passing scores, and tests must be racially neutral (Sec. 21B-30(g), (g-5)).
  • Organisations deploying AI in schools should consider the State Board's resource materials on child online safety, which may include topics like privacy protection and cyber-bullying (Sec. 27-13.3(e)).

Notable exemptions

  • From August 4, 2023 through August 31, 2025, no candidate completing a teacher preparation program or candidate subject to Section 21B-35 is required to pass a teacher performance assessment (Sec. 21B-30(f)).

Compliance steps

  • Review the State Board of Education's statewide guidance on AI use once published by July 1, 2026, and align any AI deployment in schools with its recommendations on bias, privacy, transparency, risk, and student data privacy (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)).
  • Ensure that any AI tools used in elementary and secondary education are evaluated for bias, privacy, transparency, and risk, and comply with federal and State student data privacy laws listed in the guidance (Sec. 2-3.118a(a)(3)-(4)).
  • Incorporate into the school district's Internet safety curriculum a component on recognizing and reporting online harassment and cyber-bullying, including AI-created false representations such as sexually explicit images and videos, taught at least once each school year to grades 3 through 12 (Sec. 27-13.3(c)(5)).
  • If using AI in educator testing or content area knowledge tests, monitor the State Board's website for the posted evaluation process by July 1, 2026 and ensure tests are racially neutral and meet content validity and bias standards (Sec. 21B-30(g), (g-5)).
  • Check the State Board's website for resource materials on child online safety and incorporate relevant materials into instruction (Sec. 27-13.3(e)).
  • If applicable, participate in or monitor the statewide council on AI convened by the State Superintendent (Sec. 2-3.118a(b)).
